title: Constructing Large and Structured Decoherence-Free Subspaces in Hybrid Quantum Systems
authors: Catalin-Mihai Halati, Tony Jin, Roderich Moessner
abstract: We develop a framework to construct large decoherence-free subspaces with a non-trivial structure. The construction is based on hybrid quantum systems in which quantum matter is coupled to a dissipative bosonic mode. Dissipation imposes a global constraint on the matter by selecting the matter null states in the long-time limit. The decoherence-free subspaces spanned by matter null states can exhibit exotic quantum properties and emergent symmetries that do not characterize the full Liouvillian dynamics. We show how to construct many-body operators with physically interesting null states by employing representation theory of Lie algebras. This approach allows us to choose models based on their underlying algebraic structure. We consider explicitly the example of coupling a lossy optical cavity to the directed tunneling operator of quantum particles in one-dimension. In this case, the symmetries of the decoherence-free subspace originate in an $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$ algebra, leading to an exponentially large number of steady states. We characterize the null states for both fermionic and bosonic particles, employing analytical and numerical methods. The states exhibit several properties that underline their complex quantum nature: long-range kinetic correlations and volume-law entanglement. The nonreciprocal nature of the directed tunneling dynamics leads to the emergence in the many-body regime of a symmetry-constrained Liouvillian skin effect. The open light-matter system exhibits a strong symmetry stemming from spinless $η$-pairing algebras. We show how the non-trivial properties of the long-times states emerge in the dissipative dynamics from generic initial states, by performing time-dependent matrix product state simulations. Our framework opens avenues for dissipatively engineering complex quantum correlations and harnessing nonreciprocity in a controlled manner.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical framework to engineer highly structured decoherence-free subspaces in open quantum systems by coupling matter to a dissipative bath. By leveraging representation theory of Lie algebras, the authors construct operators that enforce global constraints, leading to steady states with exotic symmetries and correlations. This method offers a controlled way to harness non-reciprocity and engineer complex quantum behavior in light-matter interactions.
main_problem: The paper develops a general framework to construct large and structured decoherence-free subspaces (DFSs) in open quantum systems.
main_result: They show that by coupling matter to a dissipative bosonic mode, one can engineer DFSs whose symmetries and properties are dictated by underlying Lie algebraic structures, leading to exotic quantum correlations.
method: The construction relies on identifying 'matter null states' imposed by dissipation, utilizing representation theory of Lie algebras to build the necessary operators.
model_or_system: The model is a hybrid quantum system coupling quantum matter (fermions or bosons) to a dissipative bosonic mode, exemplified by coupling to a lossy optical cavity and a directed tunneling operator.
key_observables: Long-range kinetic correlations, volume-law entanglement, symmetry-constrained Liouvillian skin effect, and the number of steady states.
important_parameters: The structure of the underlying Lie algebra (e.g., $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$) and the non-reciprocal nature of the coupling.
main_assumptions: The construction assumes the ability to choose an operator $O$ whose symmetries are distinct from those of the full Liouvillian dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures sketch the central ingredients, including the coupling mechanism, the resulting DFS, and evidence of non-local conserved quantities and the Liouvillian skin effect.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general framework, details the mathematical construction using Lie algebras, applies it to specific physical examples (like directed tunneling), and validates the results using analytical derivations and time-dependent MPS simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, systematic recipe for controlling quantum coherence in realistic, dissipative open systems, bridging concepts from group theory, quantum optics, and many-body physics.

The Hilbert space of the matter density matrices is sketched by a two-dimensional square for which the horizontal and verti- cal directions label the ket and bra wavefunctions. The black grid represents the subspace structure given by the presence of a strong symmetry. Red depicts the subspaces forming the DFS and blue the matter states with a finite lifetime. The photonic states are not considered in this sketch.
